outcome.technical: run-test-gate.py `_command_words` now reads an entry the way the POSIX shell that runs it does (`_proc_group.shell_invocation`). (1) shlex's POSIX escape is no longer turned off (`lexer.escape = ""` removed), so `my\ plan/x` is one word, matching how the runner's other readers split an entry (`_argv_of`, `gate_task_step`, `command_runner`, all `shlex.split`). (2) A token still holding whitespace or a quote is kept as the one word the shell reads, and is also read again as a possible shell body. Before, the re-read replaced the token, so a quoted path holding a space became two words that named nothing; that was the lw8 red on the spaced leg, where a step grading the ledger could be repeated. A re-read that cannot be split still makes the command UNSPLITTABLE. (3) The command is lexed whole, after each backslash-newline pair is removed. Lexing line by line would have made every wrapped entry unsplittable once escapes were on, and lexing whole with the pair kept would have parted a path broken across the lines, which is the unsafe direction. `_word_rels` docstring corrected: only a backslash the shell leaves in a word (single-quoted, or doubled) is read as a separator. left_out_line and its prefixes are unchanged. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md section on the left-out reading updated to say the same. tests/test_run_test_gate.py gains `_spaced_word_cases` (lw10-lw15). It builds a project path holding a space under the fixture root, so the cases go red on every leg, not only --spaced. Runs: `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_run_test_gate.py` exit 0, 1/1 files ok, 668 cases. `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --spaced tests/test_run_test_gate.py tests/test__affected_tests.py tests/test__evidence_io.py` exit 0, 3/3 files ok, 1080 cases: no case red under --spaced in any of the three suites, mine or not. `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test__deps.py` exit 0, 284 cases. `ruff check` on both .py files exit 0. Mutations, each applied once to an in-memory copy of the module (nothing in the tree was edited) and run through the suite's own `_spaced_word_cases`: escape turned off again -> lw10, lw12, lw14 red; token replaced by its re-read -> lw10, lw12, lw15 red; backslash-newline kept -> lw15 red; over-fire (any spaced word counts as left out) -> lw11, lw13 (the allow cases) red, plus lw10, lw12, lw15. The probe is <scratchpad>/mutate.py. Dependants: every existing lw/ru case of the left-out reading passes by value under both legs. lw5/lw6 (unsplittable) and lw9 (the printed line) are unchanged. drive-phase.py's read-back keys on left_out_line's two prefixes (GATE_LEFT_OUT), which are unchanged, so it still recognises the lines. The joined steps (`_affected_tests.spelled_paths`/`_words`, which already use shlex.split) and `_evidence_io.step_parts` (which reads by separator, not words) are untouched. The identity is taken over the steps before the join (run-test-gate.py `unjoined`), and `repeat_plan` maps grading names onto joined steps via step_parts, so a joined step carrying a spaced left-out entry is measured. tests/test_run_test_gate.py's importers (test_commit_task_work, test_drive_phase, test_drive_without_model) use no name this task changed. .github/sweep-costs.json, tools/affected.py, tools/verify.sh and COMPATIBILITY.md name the file by path, and those paths still hold. run-test-gate.py's importers call grades_left_out/left_out_line with unchanged signatures. `_command_words` in config/_config_rules.py is a separate function of the same name. NOT FIXED, outside my files: `_manifest_phases.gate_entry_commands` (manifest/_manifest_phases.py:1570, `lexer.escape = ""`) and `shell_words` (:1806 regex, unquoted backslash ordinary) deliberately keep a backslash as a Windows separator. So for an escaped-space path they still read two words, and `_affected_tests.gate_runs` (_affected_tests.py:973) reaches that reading when it collects the paths a task's gate runs. The left-out reading does not go through them, so this task does not depend on them. The selection reading is a second reading for that one spelling, and it is a candidate for a Faults entry if the project wants a single reading there.
outcome.descriptive: A gate entry spelling a path with a space, whether quoted, escaped, inside an sh -c body or wrapped across lines, is now recognised as naming the plan or the evidence, so it is measured rather than repeated from a stored verdict; the spaced CI leg's lw8 red is gone.
